name: org.r3js/r3
title: R3
description: Build 3D web apps: physics, audio, music, Blender import. Live edits, undo, versions, publishing.

tools.name: r3_docs_list
tools.description: Every R3 document this server can give you, IN READING ORDER, with what each one covers and how big it is. R3's documentation begins here: no model has R3 in its pretraining, and code written from tool descriptions alone saves cleanly and then silently does nothing. r3_docs_read returns one.

tools.name: r3_docs_read
tools.description:
Return one R3 document in full, or one API symbol. Paths come from r3_docs_list:
  r3_docs_read("CODE_PATTERNS.md")          how a Code component is written (reading order 1)
  r3_docs_read("PHYSICS_USAGE.md")          colliders, rigid bodies, joints
  r3_docs_read("HOWTO_PHYSICS.md")          one task step by step (how-tos: r3_docs_list)
  r3_docs_read("api")                       index of every component, system and event
  r3_docs_read("api/component/Mesh")        one component
  r3_docs_read("api/system/PhysicsRapier")  one system
  r3_docs_read("api/event/KEY_DOWN")        one event, and the data it delivers
The API reference is only ever read one symbol at a time — the whole file is too large to serve.
The call: {"path": "CODE_PATTERNS.md"} — one document per call, `path` one string (not `name` or `doc`, not an array: read several with several calls).

path.description: Which document, as one string, e.g. "CODE_PATTERNS.md", "api", "api/component/Mesh". From r3_docs_list.

tools.name: r3_whoami
tools.description: Report the R3 account you act for, how you are connected (an agent key, or an app connection made with Sign in with R3), what you are allowed to do, the account's plan (its name and how many live projects it allows and uses: a free account has 3), and whether the R3 platform is reachable. It verifies the credential end to end and names the capabilities it carries, so it is the call that confirms the account before any other tool. For an account with no project yet it gives the first step: starters to build, and projects it can remix. Tool schemas version: 9d1ebc6506e9 (the tool list you were given; r3_whoami returns the one served now).

tools.name: r3_project_create
tools.description: Create a new R3 project and save it to the user's account. Produces a complete, openable project — scene, world, camera, renderer, lighting, audio listener, music transport and OrbitControls (anyone who opens it can turn and zoom the view) — ready for components to be added. Pass `template` for a phone project (mobile-portrait / mobile-landscape) that fills the screen when published. Returns the project id, which every other project tool takes. r3_whoami confirms which account it is created in.

name.description: Project name, shown in the user's project list. Defaults to "Untitled Project". Max 120 characters.

template.description: Start from a project template instead of an Empty Project. "mobile-portrait" — A phone held upright: designed at 390×844 (~19.5:9), fills the screen when published. "mobile-landscape" — A phone held sideways: designed at 844×390 (~19.5:9), fills the screen when published. A template sets the renderer's design size and fullscreen (the canvas fills the screen it runs on; the camera follows the screen's shape, never letterboxed) and the camera's field of view for that orientation. Omit it for an Empty Project, whose renderer also fills the screen (an 800×600 fallback size, the default 75° field of view).

camera.description: Where the project's camera starts and what it looks at, e.g. framing a model you add next. Omit it for the default: (0, 5, 10) looking at the origin.

position.description: Where the camera stands (world units, Y up).

lookAt.description: The point it looks at, e.g. the centre of what you will add.

tools.name: r3_project_list
tools.description:
List the projects this R3 account can work on — its own and its teams' — last updated first, with the projectId every other project tool takes. It is how a project the user names ("my marble run") rather than giving an id is found: search for it; its projectId is what r3_project_load takes.

Search by name rather than paging: search: "marble" is matched (case-insensitively, anywhere in the name) against EVERY project by the server, not against the page you are holding. Names are not unique: when more than one project matches, the candidates' name, team and last save tell them apart, and which one is meant is the user's answer.

Each row says whose space it is in (personal, or a team by name), the account's role on it (a viewer cannot save changes), whether it is in the R3 Community, and whether you (this agent key or app connection) created it.

search.description: Match this text against project names, on the server (case-insensitive). Omit for every project.

cursor.description: Continue a previous listing: pass the nextCursor it returned, unchanged. Omit for the first page.

tools.name: r3_project_load
tools.description: List the components in an existing R3 project — what it contains and, for each one, its entityRef: the name code addresses it by (`this['mesh_cube_1']`). Read this before writing any code for a project, and after any tool call whose outcome was reported as unknown, to see what actually landed. Value components (Vector3, Color, Scalar) are not listed individually — reach them through their owner, e.g. `mesh.position.x`. Each object says which entity it belongs to (entity: {entityRef, id}, or null; r3_component_set {"entity": …} changes it), and an entityRef several components share (the same name in different entities) is listed with their ids: tools refuse that name, use the id.

projectId.description: The project to read, from r3_project_create or the R3 app.

tools.name: r3_preview_create
tools.description: Create a shareable preview link for a saved R3 project, so a person can open it in a browser and see it running. The link is valid for 7 days and does NOT make the project public; making a new one is free. It is how the user sees what you built. Takes the projectId returned by r3_project_create. Where the client shows MCP Apps (Claude on the web, desktop and mobile), the preview also shows as a playable card right in the chat, under this answer: use it when the user asks to see or play the project here or in the chat. When an R3 tab has the project open, the project's picture (its card and the link's image) is refreshed from that tab; when none has, the picture refreshes the next time the project is opened in R3.

projectId.description: The project id, as returned by r3_project_create.

tools.name: r3_preview_remove
tools.description: Remove the preview link of an R3 project: every preview link to it stops working at once (teammates' too). Only when the user asked for it, or when the preview link is what blocks an r3_project_delete the user asked for: a preview link is temporary, so it may then be removed without a separate request, and the user is told it was removed. A live project stays live; a project that was only previewed is no longer published. Deletes nothing: r3_preview_create makes a new link. A project with no open preview link is refused and left as it is. Needs the publish:preview right.

tools.name: r3_publish_live
tools.description: Publish an R3 project live: makes a RELEASE (a frozen copy) of the project as it is now and makes it the one its public live URL shows, for anyone. Only when the user asked for it. Changing the project does NOT change the live site; r3_publish_live does: on a project that is already live this is a publish update (a new release replaces the live one), and the answer names the release number and what changed since the previous live release. `note` (optional, up to 500 characters) is stored with the release. `slug` (optional, the first time a project goes live) is the project part of its public address (e.g. "my-game" for …/<handle>/my-game: letters, numbers and dashes); without it R3 uses a free address (the project's name when free) and the answer says which. Once a project has been live its address never changes. Going live the FIRST time uses one of the live-project slots of the project owner's account (an update uses none): a free account has 3 (its live pages show a small "Made with R3" badge); plans have more. When there is no room, nothing is published and the answer says how many live projects the account allows, how many are used and where the user picks a plan. It publishes every change kept so far (yours and the user's: there is nothing to save first). r3_release_list shows the releases, r3_release_rollback makes an older one live again. Needs the publish:live right.

note.description: Optional: what this release is, in a few words (up to 500 characters), e.g. "new cue and rules".

slug.description: Optional, first go-live only: the project part of the public address, e.g. "my-game" (letters, numbers and dashes). Without it R3 uses a free address and says which. A project that has been live keeps its address here (a different slug is refused): r3_publish_settings_set `address` changes it.

tools.name: r3_unpublish_live
tools.description: Take a live R3 project offline: its public live URL stops working at once, and the live-project slot it used on the plan is free again. Only when the user asked for it. Other people open a live project, so one that blocks an r3_project_delete goes offline only once the user has been asked and agreed, never as a step of the delete. Deletes nothing: the project, and any preview link, stay; r3_publish_live makes it live again. A project that is not live is refused and left as it is. Needs the publish:live right.

tools.name: r3_release_list
tools.description: List the releases of an R3 project, newest first: number, date, who made it, note, size, which one is LIVE (what the public URL shows), pinned, and releases in the trash (restorable for 7 days). Also says whether the project has saved changes that are not live yet: saving does NOT change the live site; r3_publish_live does. Read-only. Needs the project:read right.

tools.name: r3_release_rollback
tools.description: Make an earlier release of a live R3 project the one its public URL shows again (rollback, or forward again). Only when the user asked for it. The project must be live; this never uses a plan slot. A release in the trash or one marked incomplete is refused. Nothing is deleted: the release that was live stays in the list. Take the number from r3_release_list. Needs the publish:live right.

tools.name: r3_publish_settings_read
tools.description: Read the publish settings of one of the user's own R3 projects in this environment — what the app's Deploy → Settings shows: Works on (keyboard / touch / both / not tested), the SEO title and description that search engines and link previews show, how the live page starts (Start button, first click, on load), its controls and badge, its own loading logo (paid plans), and whether its music keeps playing while the phone is locked (Locked phone). Also answers a SUGGESTION for Works on, from a scan of the project's code for keyboard / touch / pointer handlers — only a suggestion. r3_publish_settings_set changes them. Needs the project:read right.

tools.name: r3_publish_settings_set
tools.description: Change publish settings of one of the user's own R3 projects in this environment — the app's Deploy → Settings. Only the settings named change (the rest stay as they are). Only when the user asked for it, or approved the text: these settings shape the PUBLIC live page — its title and description in search results and link previews (seoTitle, seoDescription), Works on (keyboard puts a "made for a keyboard" note on phones and a "desktop" badge; touch a "mobile" badge; both, both; untested none — set it only after the user confirmed it or it was tested, never from the code scan alone), how it starts (with a Start button: what runs before the Start button, startButton.before {code, physics}, and whether the project's share picture shows until Start, startButton.poster shareImage), its controls, listen (Locked phone: auto keeps the music playing with the phone locked, off stops it), and loadingLogo (paid plans only: one of the user's images, r3_image_list, shown instead of the R3 logo while the page loads; null removes it). Invalid values are refused with every problem named, and nothing is saved. The answer names what changed; open live and preview pages are told (a preview reloads, a live page offers a reload). Takes effect without a new release. `address` changes the public address of a project that is or was live (only when the user asked for it): e.g. "my-game" for r3js.org/<handle>/my-game; the old address then redirects to the new one, so links already shared keep working. Refused by name when taken, invalid or not live yet (a first go-live chooses it: r3_publish_live `slug`). Needs the publish:live right. R3 admins only: `gallery` features, hides or sets the example prompt of a project in the landing gallery (any member's project; send it without `settings` for a project that is not yours).

settings.description: Only the settings to change, e.g. {"worksOn": "keyboard", "seoDescription": "…"}.

worksOn.description: What the project works on: keyboard (desktop only — phone visitors see a "made for a keyboard" note and the project gets a "desktop" badge), touch ("mobile" badge), both, or untested (no note, no badge).

seoTitle.description: The title search engines and link previews show (up to 200 characters).

seoDescription.description: The description search engines and link previews show (up to 500 characters). Empty, they show a generic line.

autoStart.description: How the live page starts: auto (the default: a Start button only when the project has sound or physics, else it starts on load), startButton (always a Start button), firstGesture (the first click anywhere), load (on load: physics and code only, no audio).

before.description: What runs BEFORE the Start button (startButton and firstGesture modes), e.g. {"code": true} so code that builds the scene runs on load; the press starts the rest. Code and physics only: audio and music always wait for the press. Default: nothing.

poster.description: What the page shows before Start: scene (the default) or shareImage (the project's share picture fills the page behind the Start button until Start runs; with no share picture, the scene).

controls.description: The always-visible pause / resume buttons on the live page.

attribution.description: The "Made with R3" badge: always shown on a free account's live projects; on a paid plan it is off unless show is true.

loadingLogo.description: Paid plans only: the user's own logo on the loading screen of the live page and its preview links, instead of the R3 logo. On a free account it is refused; when a plan ends the R3 logo shows again and the choice is kept.

imageId.description: One of the user's images (r3_image_list: PNG, JPEG or WebP up to 1 MB), or null for the R3 logo.

alt.description: What a screen reader says for the logo (up to 120 characters; empty = the project's name).

listen.description: Locked phone: auto (the default: when the project has music, a Song, Pattern, Beat or DrumGrid, the music started on the live page keeps playing with the phone locked, the project's name and share picture on the lock screen) or off (the music stops with the page, as on any web page). No button of its own: the page's Music control does it.

gallery.description: R3 admins only: the landing gallery, e.g. {"featured": true} or {"examplePrompt": "…"}.

featured.description: true pins the project to the top of the landing gallery; false unpins it.

hidden.description: true keeps the project out of the landing gallery (its live page stays); false shows it again.

examplePrompt.description: The exact prompt that made this project, shown with a "Made by R3" label and a Copy prompt button (up to 500 characters; empty clears it). Only on a project an R3 account owns.

address.description: The new project part of the live address, e.g. "my-game" (letters, numbers and dashes). Only for a project that is or was live; the old address redirects to the new one.

tools.name: r3_project_rename
tools.description:
Rename a project: the name shown in the user's project list, the editor's title and the live page. The same change as clicking the title in the R3 editor, kept at once in the project's live copy (every open R3 tab shows it).

The public address does not change: a preview or live link keeps working. Scripts are not affected (they never address the project by name). Renaming a COMPONENT is not this tool: that is done in the R3 editor.

projectId.description: The project to rename, from r3_project_list or r3_project_create.

name.description: The new name. Leading and trailing spaces are trimmed. Max 120 characters.

tools.name: r3_project_remix
tools.description:
Remix a project: copy the published release of a project into a NEW private project in this account. The source needs its Remixable switch on (any member may switch it on for their project, in the R3 app); someone else's must also be in the Community or live, while the owner or a team editor may remix it even when private. The files it uses are copied into the account's own lists, the new project carries a credit line naming the original and its author, and its code starts held until Run is pressed in the R3 editor. The original is not changed.

Limits: 20 remixes per account in 24 hours and 5 per agent key in an hour; one remix copies at most 50.0MB of files; a project with videos cannot be remixed yet.

Returns the new project id, which every other project tool takes, the credit, and notes on anything that could not be copied. r3_editor_open opens it in the user's R3 tab and r3_preview_create makes a private link to show it.

projectId.description: The project to remix: its id from its R3 page, r3_project_list, or the user.

name.description: The new project's name. Defaults to "<original name> (remix)", made unique in this account. Max 120 characters.

tools.name: r3_project_delete
tools.description: Permanently delete an R3 project. With the project:delete:created right (on by default), only a project YOU created (this agent key or app connection) — use it to clean up your own abandoned attempts; the user's own projects and other agents' are refused. With project:delete:owned, any project the user owns, and only when the user asked for it: pass owned: true for a project you did not create (an app connection is then asked for that right). A published project (live, or with an open preview link) is refused: it must be taken offline first. If the refusal is for a preview link (temporary, 7 days), it may be removed without a separate request (r3_preview_remove) and the delete tried again; the user is then told it was removed. If the project is live, other people can open it: it goes offline only once the user has been asked and agreed, never as a step of the delete. This is irreversible: there is no trash and no undo.

projectId.description: The project id to delete: one you created, or (with project:delete:owned) any project the user owns.

owned.description: true when the project is one of the user's own, not one you created: it needs project:delete:owned. Only when the user asked to delete it. Leave out for a project you created.

tools.name: r3_factory_list
tools.description: List the R3 factories available to r3_factory_run, with each one's options, types and defaults. A factory builds a complete, correctly-wired object — a cube is a mesh plus geometry plus material plus colour, already connected. Call this before r3_factory_run if you are unsure of a factory name or its options.

factory.description: Optional: return only this factory, e.g. "Cube". Omit for all of them.

tools.name: r3_factory_run
tools.description: Add an object to an existing R3 project — a cube, sphere, terrain, lighting, a physics body, and so on. The call: {"projectId": "…", "factory": "Cube", "params": {"position": {"y": 2}}, "name": "Crate"} — `factory` is a name from r3_factory_list (not `type`), `params` ONE object of its options (left out: every default). Each factory builds a complete, correctly-wired object (mesh + geometry + material + colour, already connected), so you never assemble components by hand. Kept at once in the project's live copy: every R3 tab with the project open shows it now, no editor needed and nothing to save (r3_editor_create is the same tool). The answer says what was kept and its seq. "name" names what you make ("Leg front left" → entityRef leg_front_left): the primary component (a cube's Mesh, a light), unique in the project (a name already used gets _2); its geometry and material take it too (leg_front_left_geometry, leg_front_left_material). Name parts when you make them (a later rename: r3_component_rename). Lighting takes no "name" (it makes several parts; rename each with r3_component_set afterwards); every other factory does. "StudioLighting" lights a scene the way a photo studio does: one of R3's built-in HDR environments (studio, sunset, sky) as the scene's environment, so metal and glossy materials reflect, plus a key light. Use r3_factory_list to see the factories and their options.

projectId.description: The project to add to, from r3_project_create.

params.description: Factory options as ONE object, e.g. {"color": 16711680, "position": {"y": 2}} (a position / scale is an object {x, y, z}, not an array). Every option has a default. Color is a packed RGB integer. Rotations are in RADIANS, not degrees: a quarter turn is Math.PI/2 ≈ 1.5708 (the R3 Inspector shows rotations in degrees: 90°).

name.description: The name of what you make, e.g. "Leg front left" (at most 120 characters). Its entityRef, the name code uses, follows from it (leg_front_left). Not for Lighting.

tools.name: r3_code_write
tools.description:
Add or replace a Code component: JavaScript a project runs. It runs on ONE event you choose (`event`): RENDER_BEFORE (default) every frame, for movement (held keys: this.keysPressed); KEY_DOWN / KEY_UP once per press / release; MOUSE_CLICK, SWIPE, MUSIC_BEAT, PHYSICS_COLLISION, UI_CLICK (a screen button) once per happening. A script per event: r3_docs_read("HOWTO_CODE_EVENTS.md"). Kept at once in the live copy every open R3 tab runs (r3_editor_code: the same tool).

r3_project_load names the entityRefs; r3_docs_read("CODE_PATTERNS.md") is the API (a guessed one silently does nothing).

The code is a function body:
```js
this.update = function(data) {
  this['mesh_cube_1'].rotation.y += data.delta;
};
return {update: this.update};   // REQUIRED (also start, dispose) — nothing runs without it
```
Reach a component as `this['<entityRef>']`, infrastructure with this.getProject() / getScene() / getCamera() / getWorld() / getAudioListener() / getEntityInstance(). Anything else returned is an api other scripts call: `this['<entityRef>'].api.<name>(...)`. Code that creates things (scene objects, timers, listeners) frees them in a returned `dispose`: R3 calls it on re-save, Stop and delete.

No getComponentByRef, this.state, this.getSibling or R3 global: code using them is REFUSED.

EVENTS (by NAME; default RENDER_BEFORE): RENDER_BEFORE, RENDER_AFTER, KEY_DOWN, KEY_UP, MOUSE_DOWN, MOUSE_UP, MOUSE_MOVE, MOUSE_WHEEL, MOUSE_CLICK, TOUCH_START, TOUCH_MOVE, TOUCH_END, TOUCH_CANCEL, SWIPE, MUSIC_BEAT, MUSIC_BAR, SONG_CUE, PHYSICS_COLLISION, UI_CLICK. Their `data` (mouse: nested, -1..+1): the how-to's table.

Pass entityRef + baseVersion (r3_code_read's codeVersion) to REPLACE a script; name (or neither) to create one. Never merged: an older one is refused with the current code.

PATCH a long script: replacements [{old, new, count?}] + baseSha256 (r3_code_read's), no code; all or nothing, each old found exactly count (default 1) times; ≤ 200 replacements, 60000 chars.

projectId.description: The project to write into, from r3_project_create or r3_project_load.

code.description: The JavaScript. A function body that returns {start, update} — see the description. Omit it when you send replacements.

event.description: Which event runs it, by NAME: RENDER_BEFORE, RENDER_AFTER, KEY_DOWN, KEY_UP, MOUSE_DOWN, MOUSE_UP, MOUSE_MOVE, MOUSE_WHEEL, MOUSE_CLICK, TOUCH_START, TOUCH_MOVE, TOUCH_END, TOUCH_CANCEL, SWIPE, MUSIC_BEAT, MUSIC_BAR, SONG_CUE, PHYSICS_COLLISION, UI_CLICK. Default RENDER_BEFORE on create; left unchanged on update.

name.description: Label for a NEW Code component, e.g. "Spin". Cannot be combined with entityRef.

entityRef.description: The entityRef of an EXISTING Code component to replace, as reported by r3_project_load. Cannot be combined with name.

componentId.description: Or the id of the EXISTING Code component to replace (instead of entityRef).

baseVersion.description: REQUIRED with entityRef: the codeVersion r3_code_read answered for that script. A write on an older version is refused with the current code, never merged. Leave it out when creating (0 also means "a new script").

baseSha256.description: With replacements only: the sha256 r3_code_read answered for the script (of its WHOLE code) at baseVersion.

replacements.description: Instead of code: exact replacements on the script at baseVersion, in order, all or nothing (at most 200, 60000 characters of old + new in all).

old.description: Exact text in the script (whitespace and line breaks count).

new.description: What replaces it (empty deletes it). Taken literally.

count.description: How many times old occurs, all replaced (default 1).

tools.name: r3_code_read
tools.description:
Read back what a Code component actually contains — its full JavaScript source and the event it runs on. r3_code_write reports what it wrote; this reports what is there.

Use it before replacing a script, so an edit builds on the real source instead of overwriting it blind, and after a write whose reply you did not see, to confirm what landed. Call it with NO entityRefs to get every Code component in the project — that is how you find a script again when you never received the entityRef for it.

Each script comes back with its codeVersion: pass it as r3_code_write's baseVersion. The event comes back as a NAME (RENDER_BEFORE, KEY_DOWN, …), which is the same form r3_code_write takes, so you can hand it straight back. r3_component_read reports the same field as a raw number and omits any source over 2000 characters; this is the tool for reading code.

Name ONE entityRef to read it in pages (offset / length): every script comes back with totalChars, the sha256 of its WHOLE source, and truncated / nextOffset. When truncated is true you have only part of it: read on from nextOffset, join the pages and check the sha256 before writing it back. Reading several, a body longer than one page is left out WHOLE and named with its size — never cut silently, because a partial script written back would delete the rest of it. An entityRef that does not exist is named and the others are still read.

Name the project's Help (its entityRef) to read its markdown the same way — whole or in pages, with the codeVersion r3_help_write takes as baseVersion.

projectId.description: The project to read from, from r3_project_create or r3_project_load.

entityRefs.description: Which Code components to read, e.g. ["spin"]. Omit for ALL of them. Up to 50 per call.

offset.description: Where to start reading, in characters (default 0). For the next page pass the nextOffset of the previous answer.

length.description: How many characters to read at most (default and maximum 60000; 8000 in an R3 Builder session). A page ends on a whole line when it can.

tools.name: r3_help_write
tools.description:
Set the instructions that ship WITH a project — controls, what to press, what it does. R3 renders them in a modal behind a floating "?" button and the H key, in the editor and in the live portal alike, so whoever opens your preview link can read them. This is the built-in surface for that, so a Code component needs no overlay of its own.

The body is markdown — headings, bullets, `code`, links: the controls as a player needs them, e.g. "## Controls\n\n- `Space` — jump".

A project has ONE help. Call this again and it replaces the text rather than adding a second. REPLACING needs baseVersion, the codeVersion r3_code_read gives for the Help (name its entityRef; it reads the whole markdown, in pages if long): text is never merged, so a write on an older version is refused with the current text. The first Help needs none. The optional title is the modal's heading ("Controls", "How to play"); leave it out to keep "Help".

Kept at once in the project's live copy: every R3 tab with the project open shows it now. The result gives you the component's entityRef — pass that to r3_component_set to change the trigger key, move or hide the button, or have the help open automatically on load.

projectId.description: The project to write into, from r3_project_create or r3_project_load.

markdown.description: The help text, as markdown. Replaces whatever is there.

title.description: Heading shown at the top of the modal, e.g. "Controls". Default "Help".

baseVersion.description: REQUIRED when the project already has a Help: its codeVersion, from r3_code_read (entityRefs: [its entityRef]). For the first Help leave it out (0 also means "no Help yet").

tools.name: r3_component_set
tools.description:
Set one or more properties on a component that already exists in a project — a material's roughness, a mesh's position, which material a mesh uses. Kept at once in the project's live copy: every R3 tab with the project open shows it, nothing to save (r3_editor_set is the same tool); the answer gives its seq.

Call: {"projectId": "…", "entityRef": "mesh_cube_1", "properties": {"roughness": 0.25}}: `properties` is ONE object (not `values`, not {property, value} pairs).

Components are addressed by entityRef (r3_project_load lists them); one several components share is refused with them: pass componentId (or the id as a reference). {"entity": "<an Entity's entityRef>"} puts it in that Entity; null takes it out.

Properties come in four shapes and the value you pass differs:
  • plain value  — {"roughness": 0.25}, {"visible": false}
  • value component (position / rotation / scale / color / size …) — pass an OBJECT of just the keys to change: {"position": {"y": 2}} leaves x and z alone. Vector3 has x/y/z, Color has r/g/b/a (0..1), Scalar has value. An EMPTY slot (a rigid body's centerOfMass is empty until set) is made from the fields given: {"centerOfMass": {"z": -0.3, "mass": 8}}; the fields not named keep their defaults. Rotations are in RADIANS, not degrees: a quarter turn is Math.PI/2 ≈ 1.5708 (the R3 Inspector shows rotations in degrees: 90°).
  • reference to another component — pass that component's entityRef as a string: {"material": "material_cube_1"}, or null to clear it.
  • list of references (a mesh's materials) — pass an ARRAY of entityRefs: {"materials": ["mat_a", "mat_b"]}. The array REPLACES the whole list, in the order given — it does NOT append, so name every component you want in it; [] empties the list. The answer shows the list before and after.

Several properties in one call apply all-or-nothing. An unknown property is refused with the valid names. Rename (name / entityRef) with r3_component_rename.

Giving a VehicleWheel its mesh or vehicle measures the wheel from that mesh, as the R3 editor does (Configure from Mesh: radius, connectionPoint, axle); a value named in the same call is kept. Giving a ColliderCuboid / Sphere / Cylinder / Capsule its mesh fits it to that mesh (Fit to Mesh: size, and position on the mesh's centre); giving it only a rigidBody fits the values still at their defaults. The answer says what was measured or fitted and what was kept (PHYSICS_USAGE.md → Vehicles).

Moving or scaling a Mesh keeps what the editor derives from it: a SCALE change re-fits every Cuboid / Sphere / Cylinder / Capsule collider fitted to that mesh (size and offset); moving or scaling a wheel's mesh re-measures the wheel; scaling a vehicle's chassis mesh also carries the wheels' suspensionRestLength and maxSuspensionTravel by the new / old scale on the up axis. The answer lists each.

A Mesh's rotation and quaternion are one orientation held twice: set ONE of them and the other follows (both in one call must agree, or the call is refused).

Changing the parent of a Mesh / Empty / Points / Line ({"parent": "root_empty"}, or null for the scene) keeps it where it is in the world, as the R3 editor's re-parent does: its position, rotation (and quaternion) and scale are rewritten to the values local to the new parent, and the answer lists them. A position, rotation / quaternion or scale given in the SAME call is the new LOCAL value under the new parent, taken as given; the fields not given keep the world place. Under a NON-UNIFORMLY scaled parent a rotated part cannot keep its shape (it would shear): that re-parent is refused unless you give rotation and scale yourself.

projectId.description: The project the component is in, from r3_project_create or r3_project_load.

entityRef.description: Which component to change, as reported by r3_project_load, e.g. "mesh_cube_1".

componentId.description: Or its id (r3_project_load) — exactly one of entityRef / componentId.

properties.description: What to set: ONE object of property → value, e.g. {"roughness": 0.25, "position": {"y": 2}, "material": "material_cube_1"}. Required.

tools.name: r3_component_read
tools.description:
Read back what components actually hold — a material's colour and roughness, a mesh's position, which material it uses. r3_project_load gives you the names; this gives you the values behind them.

Pass SEVERAL entityRefs in one call — telling six similarly-named materials apart is the case this exists for, and it is one round trip rather than six. One component: entityRef: "mesh_cube_1" (r3_component_set's name for it) works too.

What comes back is exactly what r3_component_set takes, so read → change → write needs no translation: value components are expanded inline ({"position": {"x": 0, "y": 2, "z": 0}}), references are the target's entityRef as a string (or null when empty), and lists of references are arrays of entityRefs. Use it before any relative change ("20% brighter", "move it up by one"), and after a write to confirm what landed.

Bulk data — mesh vertex arrays and anything else megabyte-sized — is NOT returned. Every property left out is listed with the reason, so an omission is never silent.

Each answer says which entity the component belongs to (entity: {entityRef, id}, or null). An id works in place of an entityRef; an entityRef several components hold (the same name in different entities) is not guessed: it is reported with each holder's id.

An entityRef that does not exist is reported by name and the rest are still read. Value components (a Vector3, a Color) are not read on their own: ask for the component that owns them.

projectId.description: The project the components are in, from r3_project_create or r3_project_load.

entityRefs.description: Which components to read, as reported by r3_project_load: an ARRAY, e.g. ["mesh_cube_1", "material_cube_1"]. Up to 50 per call.

tools.name: r3_terrain_height
tools.description:
How high the ground of a heightfield terrain is at the world (x, z) positions you ask, exactly as physics and the drawn terrain have it, plus the terrain's lowest and highest point, centre, size and footprint. Use it to place something ON a terrain: an object stands on the ground at (x, z) when its lowest point is at the returned y (a vehicle: its wheels' bottom); the returned ground normal says how steep it is there. One call takes up to 100 points; with none it describes the terrain only.

`terrain` is the terrain's Mesh, GeometryHeightfield or ColliderHeightfield (entityRef or id); leave it out when the project has one terrain.

It reads the user's open R3 editor when it has the project (the terrain as on screen, a heightmap image included), else the saved project. A terrain shaped by a heightmap IMAGE needs the project open in R3 (r3_editor_open), because only a browser decodes the image. Read-only: nothing is changed.

projectId.description: The project, from r3_project_list or r3_project_create.

terrain.description: The terrain: its Mesh, GeometryHeightfield or ColliderHeightfield, by entityRef or id. Optional when the project has one terrain.

points.description: World positions to sample, e.g. [{"x": 0, "z": 12.5}]. Up to 100.

tools.name: r3_component_bounds
tools.description: The size and place of meshes and imported models, in R3 units (metres): the world-space box around each (min, max, size, centre), the mesh's scale, rotation and parents applied. Name a Mesh, or the root Empty of a Blender model (r3_blender_import makes one, named "<model>_root"), and the box covers it and every mesh under it, with each part listed. Use it before scaling or placing anything relative to its size: to stand a model on the ground, move it so its min.y is the ground height (r3_terrain_height on a terrain); to make it 2 m long, scale by 2 / size. Each answer also gives the project camera's position and lookAt that show it whole on any screen, a phone held upright included: use it to frame a model. Several in one call (up to 20). Works with no R3 tab open, from the project as it is kept; read-only.

projectId.description: The project, from r3_project_list or r3_project_create.

entityRefs.description: Meshes or model root Empties to measure, by entityRef (r3_project_load lists them) or id, e.g. ["truck_root"]. Up to 20.

tools.name: r3_component_add
tools.description:
Add one component of ANY registered type — a collider, a rigid body, a joint, a light, a material, a geometry … — to a saved R3 project, with its values and references set before it is created. Kept at once in the project's live copy: every R3 tab with the project open shows it now, no editor needed and nothing to save (r3_editor_add_component is the same tool). Use r3_factory_run for a ready-made object (a cube, a physics sphere …).

`type` is the short type name, e.g. "ColliderCuboid" (an unknown type is refused with the list). `values` take r3_component_set's shapes: a plain value {"friction": 0.2}; a value component as the keys to set {"halfExtents": {"x": 2, "y": 0.5, "z": 1}}; a reference as the target's entityRef or id {"rigidBody": "rigidbody_dynamic_1"} — a component of THIS project, of a type the slot accepts; "name" names it (a name already used is kept as its label, and its entityRef gets a suffix, e.g. hull_2: the answer says so); "entity" puts it in an Entity (its value components join too). A type that cannot exist without an option (an Audio / AudioPositional / Texture's "url") takes it in values too, and is refused without it. A Code component's code is r3_code_write's. A VehicleWheel added with a mesh is measured from it (Configure from Mesh: radius, connectionPoint, axle), and a ColliderCuboid / Sphere / Cylinder / Capsule with a mesh (its own or its rigid body's) is fitted to it (Fit to Mesh: size, and position on the mesh's centre), only the values you did not pass; the answer says what (PHYSICS_USAGE.md → Vehicles).

tools.name: r3_editor_open
tools.description:
Open a project in the R3 editor the user has open in their browser (their most recently used R3 tab) and focus it, so they see it. A project already open there is just focused (never reloaded). It is how the user gets to see the project you are working on, and how a tab gets the project r3_editor_inspect reads. To show the project to the user right here in the chat, use r3_preview_create instead (a playable card in the chat where the client shows MCP Apps, else a link).

The same access rules as opening it by hand: the user's own projects, their teams', and public ones. The editor holds up to 4 projects; at that limit it refuses. Nothing is saved or changed. When no R3 tab is open, the answer (`notOpen`) says nothing was opened, where the user opens R3, and that r3_preview_create shows the project without one.

projectId.description: The project to open, from r3_project_list or r3_project_create.

tools.name: r3_editor_inspect
tools.description:
Read what components hold RIGHT NOW in an R3 tab that has the project open: runtime values included — a moving body's position while the project runs. Use it to debug live behaviour. It needs a tab with the project open (r3_editor_open opens one). r3_component_read reads the kept values without a tab.

Select with any of: `ids` (component ids from r3_project_load), `type` ("Mesh", "RigidBodyDynamic", …) and `entityRef`; they combine. `fields` keeps only the properties you name (e.g. ["position", "rotation"]). At most 50 components per call; a larger answer is refused with how to narrow it.

Values are in r3_component_read's shape (value components inline, references as entityRefs), so they can be handed to r3_component_set. The project must be open in the editor (r3_editor_open opens it). Read-only: nothing is changed.

Script problems: `scriptDiagnostics` lists the recent errors and warnings of the Code components read (compile / start / runtime errors, warnings such as AmbiguousEntityRefError), each with its name, message, count and last time, since the last Run. Inspect type "Code" after r3_editor_run to see whether your scripts run cleanly; null means the tab does not report them.

A script's state: `api: true` (or `{"path": "state.ships", "depth": 2}`) with the script's `entityRef` (or one id) reads what that Code component's code returned besides start / update / dispose (its `api`: the values and functions it exposes), as the running script holds it now, as plain JSON (functions as {"$function": name}; deeper than depth 4 (at most 8), past 100 items or very long text is cut and marked). Reading never runs the script. Use it after r3_editor_step or r3_editor_run to check game state (a score, a wave, a list of enemies) instead of writing it to a ScreenText; return what you want to read from the script.

projectId.description: The project, open in the user's editor.

type.description: Only components of this type, e.g. "Mesh" or "R3ComponentMesh".

entityRef.description: Only the component with this entityRef.

api.description: Read ONE script's returned api instead of component values: true, or {path?, depth?}; name the script with entityRef or one id.

path.description: A part of the api, e.g. "state.ships.0" (object keys / array indexes).

tools.name: r3_editor_set
tools.description:
The same tool as r3_component_set (this is its older name): change properties of a component, kept at once in the project's live copy: every R3 tab with the project open shows it now, no editor needed and nothing to save.

Name the component with componentId or entityRef. `values` take r3_component_set's shapes: a plain value {"roughness": 0.25}; a value component as an object of the keys to change {"position": {"y": 2}} (an EMPTY slot, e.g. a rigid body's centerOfMass, is made from the fields given: {"centerOfMass": {"z": -0.3, "mass": 8}}); a reference as the target's entityRef {"material": "material_cube_1"} (null clears it); a list of references as an array of entityRefs (it REPLACES the list). All-or-nothing: an unknown name is refused with the valid ones. A Code component's code is r3_editor_code's. Rotations are in RADIANS, not degrees: a quarter turn is Math.PI/2 ≈ 1.5708 (the R3 Inspector shows rotations in degrees: 90°).

tools.name: r3_editor_code
tools.description: The same tool as r3_code_write (this is its older name): replace a Code component's code, kept at once in the project's live copy: every R3 tab with the project open runs the new code now, no editor needed and nothing to save. Name it with componentId or entityRef and pass baseVersion, the codeVersion r3_code_read answered: code is never merged, so on an older version it is refused with the current code and version (apply your change to that and call again). A long script can be PATCHED instead: replacements + baseSha256, as r3_code_write takes them. The code is a FUNCTION BODY (a top-level `return {start, update};`); read r3_docs_read("CODE_PATTERNS.md") for the R3 APIs. A syntax error or an R3 API that does not exist is refused before anything is kept.

code.description: The whole new code (a function body). Omit it when you send replacements.

baseVersion.description: REQUIRED: the codeVersion r3_editor_inspect gave for this Code component (the version your code builds on); null for one never saved (codeVersion null).

baseSha256.description: With replacements only: the sha256 r3_code_read answered for the script (of its WHOLE code) at baseVersion.

replacements.description: Instead of code: exact replacements on the script at baseVersion, in order, all or nothing (at most 200, 60000 characters of old + new in all).

old.description: Exact text in the script (whitespace and line breaks count).

new.description: What replaces it (empty deletes it). Taken literally.

count.description: How many times old occurs, all replaced (default 1).

tools.name: r3_editor_create
tools.description: The same tool as r3_factory_run (this is its older name): add an object — a cube, sphere, light, physics body … — kept at once in the project's live copy: every R3 tab with the project open shows it now, no editor needed and nothing to save. r3_factory_list lists the factories and their params.

params.description: Factory options, e.g. {"color": 16711680, "position": {"y": 2}}. Color is a packed RGB integer. Rotations are in RADIANS, not degrees: a quarter turn is Math.PI/2 ≈ 1.5708 (the R3 Inspector shows rotations in degrees: 90°).

name.description: The name of what you make, e.g. "Leg front left" (r3_factory_run's name).

tools.name: r3_editor_add_component
tools.description:
The same tool as r3_component_add (this is its older name): add one component of ANY registered type — a collider, a rigid body, a joint, a light, a material, a geometry … — with its values and references set before it is created, kept at once in the project's live copy: every R3 tab with the project open shows it now, no editor needed and nothing to save. Use r3_editor_create for a ready-made object.

`type` is the short type name, e.g. "ColliderCuboid" (an unknown type is refused with the list). `values` take r3_component_set's shapes: a plain value {"friction": 0.2}; a value component as the keys to set {"halfExtents": {"x": 2, "y": 0.5, "z": 1}}; a reference as the target's entityRef or id {"rigidBody": "rigidbody_dynamic_1"} — a component of THIS project, of a type the slot accepts. Example — swap a rigid body's collider: add a ColliderCuboid with {"rigidBody": …, "halfExtents": …}, then r3_editor_delete the old collider (mode "one").

tools.name: r3_editor_delete
tools.description: Delete components from the project the user has OPEN in their R3 editor, exactly as the editor's delete dialog asks it — in TWO calls. First call WITHOUT `confirm`: it returns the plan and changes nothing — the selected components, what only they use (their geometry, material, colliders …), an Entity's members, the modes on offer and a planToken. Then call again with the same componentIds and confirm: {"mode": …, "planToken": …}: "one" deletes only the selection, "with_dependents" also what only it uses, "bundle" (one Entity) the entity with its members. The mode is the user's choice, unless they already said. If the project changes in between, the confirm is refused: plan again. Only when the user asked for it. The confirmed delete is kept at once in the project's live copy (every open R3 tab shows it; no editor is needed); R3 keeps what was deleted in the project's trash. The children of a deleted Empty or Mesh keep their place in the world, as the editor's delete does (their numbers become the scene's; the answer lists them). A project itself is never deleted here. Needs the editor:dispose capability.

componentIds.description: The ids of the components to delete (r3_editor_inspect / r3_project_load).

confirm.description: Leave out to get the plan; give it to delete what the plan named.

mode.description: one | with_dependents | bundle — one of the plan's modes.

planToken.description: The planToken the plan call returned.

tools.name: r3_editor_undo
tools.description:
Undo the last change YOU (this agent key or app connection) made to a project: everything one of your tool calls changed is undone together, and the user sees it at once in any R3 tab that has the project open. Use it when your own change was wrong or the user asks you to take it back. It never undoes the user's changes or another agent's: only yours. `count` undoes your last few changes, newest first.

If someone else changed the same thing after you, that change of yours is SKIPPED: nothing is changed, the answer says who changed what, and that change of yours is dropped from your history (the next call takes the one before it). Their change stands: setting your old value back over theirs is the user's decision, not this tool's.

`redo: true` puts back what you undid (until you make a new change). Needs project:write (and code:write to undo a change to code).

count.description: How many of your changes to undo (or redo), newest first (default 1, at most 20).

redo.description: true: redo what you undid instead of undoing.

tools.name: r3_release_restore
tools.description:
Put a project's working copy back the way one of its releases (saved versions) had it: components added since are removed, removed ones come back, values and scripts go back to that version (each script as a new version on top of the current one), and the name. The user sees it at once in any R3 tab that has the project open. Only when the user asked for it.

Two steps: WITHOUT planToken it changes nothing and says what restoring would change, with a planToken; the same call WITH that planToken, once the user has seen the plan and agreed, restores. If the project changed in between, nothing is changed and the new plan comes back.

The whole restore is ONE change of yours: r3_editor_undo takes it back. It never changes which release is LIVE (what the public URL shows): that is r3_release_rollback. The release number comes from r3_release_list. Needs project:write (and code:write when scripts change).

releaseNumber.description: The release to restore the working copy to (r3_release_list).

planToken.description: The planToken the first call answered; only when the user agreed to that plan.

tools.name: r3_editor_run
tools.description: Press the Run buttons of the user's open R3 editor: start physics, code, audio and music (all of them, or the ones named in `systems`), exactly as the user's own click does — a paused simulation resumes. Use it to TEST what you built: run it, then look with r3_editor_capture and read live values with r3_editor_inspect. Changes nothing saved. It shows the named project first (focused, scrolled into view): the systems start for every project open in that tab, but only a project on screen moves. The scene only moves while that tab is in front: a browser pauses a background tab, and the answer then says the scene is NOT advancing. While physics runs, edits wait until Stop: stop before a visual change (lights, materials …), then capture or run again. With no R3 tab that has the project open, nothing runs and the answer says what to do (`notOpen`). Needs the editor:run right.

projectId.description: A project open in the user's editor (r3_whoami lists them).

systems.description: Which of the editor's Run / Stop buttons: physics, code, audio, music. Leave out for all of them.

tools.name: r3_editor_stop
tools.description: Press the Stop buttons of the user's open R3 editor: stop physics, code, audio and music (all of them, or the ones named in `systems`), exactly as the user's own click does. Stopping physics puts every body back where it was placed. It stops every project open in that tab. Changes nothing saved. Needs the editor:run right.

projectId.description: A project open in the user's editor (r3_whoami lists them).

systems.description: Which of the editor's Run / Stop buttons: physics, code, audio, music. Leave out for all of them.

tools.name: r3_editor_step
tools.description:
Advance a project open in the user's R3 editor by a number of frames, run by R3 itself: scripts (RENDER_BEFORE with data.delta = dt), physics and the music clock move on exactly as in real frames, and one picture is drawn at the end. It works in a HIDDEN (background) tab, where the browser stops the scene: that is what it is for, testing motion (falling blocks, a jump, a song section) deterministically. `keys` holds keys across the frames (this.keysPressed and KEY_DOWN / KEY_UP, as if pressed). The answer says what happened: frames run, game time, the systems that ran, the keys, the music, script errors and console lines.

The loop: Stop → edit → Run → step → inspect / capture. Edits made during a run wait until Stop (the run lock), so stop, make the change, r3_editor_run, then step; read values with r3_editor_inspect (`api` reads what a script returned), look with r3_editor_capture. Start the systems with r3_editor_run first: a step only advances what runs. In a visible tab whose project runs live a step is refused unless physics is paused there (it would run twice as fast in the user's view). At most 600 frames per call (10 s at 1/60 s): step again for longer, it goes on where it stopped. Sound is muted while stepping. Nothing saved changes. Needs the editor:run right.

projectId.description: A project open in the user's editor (r3_whoami lists them).

frames.description: How many frames to run, 1..600. For longer, call again.

dt.description: Seconds per frame, more than 0 and at most 0.05 (default 1/60).

keys.description: Keys held during the step: a code ("KeyW") for the whole step, or {"code": "Space", "from": 10, "to": 20} for frames 10 to 19.

from.description: The frame it goes down before (0-based; default 0).

to.description: The frame it goes up before (default: the end of the step).

tools.name: r3_editor_capture
tools.description: Capture the canvas of a project open in the user's R3 editor — the scene as it looks NOW, running physics included — and LOOK at it: the answer is an image. Call it after a visual change (r3_editor_set, r3_editor_create, r3_editor_code …) to check what you built, and after r3_editor_run to see it move. By default (`camera: "editor"`) it is what the user sees: the editor's view camera, edit aids included. `camera: "project"` takes it through the project's own camera instead, with no edit aids, as a visitor sees it: use that to check a camera or a camera script. At most 1280 px each way (`width`, default 1024); a JPEG. With no R3 tab that has the project open, the answer has no picture and says what to do (`notOpen`: open it in R3, or r3_preview_create). Needs project:read.

projectId.description: A project open in the user's editor (r3_whoami lists them).

width.description: The picture's largest width in px, 64..1280 (default 1024); it keeps the canvas's aspect and is never scaled up.

camera.description: Whose view: "editor" (default) = the editor's view camera the user looks through, edit aids included; "project" = the project's own camera, no edit aids, as a visitor sees it (check a camera script with it).

tools.name: r3_editor_set_preview_image
tools.description: Use what the project's camera shows NOW, in the user's open R3 editor, as the project's share image: the picture its live page, link previews (social cards) and the showcase show, used when the project is next published (r3_publish_live, or Publish update in the editor). The editor waits until the scene's textures have loaded and takes it without edit aids (no grid, gizmos or outlines), as a visitor sees it; the answer is the picture it set. It is for once the project looks right (r3_editor_capture shows it beforehand), or when the user asks for a new picture. A live page keeps the share image of its live release until that next publish. Needs a tab with the project open and project:write.

projectId.description: A project open in the user's editor (r3_whoami lists them).

tools.name: r3_entity_list
tools.description: List this R3 account's entity templates: reusable bundles (a ship, a lamp post) saved from an Entity in a project, each with its current version and member count. community: true lists everyone's public templates instead. r3_entity_read shows one template's members and versions; r3_entity_import puts a copy into a project; r3_entity_save_template saves an Entity of a project as a template.

cursor.description: Continue a list: the nextCursor of the previous page.

search.description: Only templates whose name matches, searched across all of them.

community.description: true lists the PUBLIC templates of every user instead of this account's own.

tools.name: r3_entity_read
tools.description: Read one entity template (this account's, or a public one): its current version, the members of the version read (type, name, entityRef; value components such as positions and colours are counted, they belong to their member), the shared code modules it imports, and its recent versions with their notes. version reads an older version, and the references its members hold to components outside the Entity (outsideReferences: infrastructure such as the scene or camera is expected and re-bound on import; anything else is left empty by an import into another project). The current version is the baseVersion r3_entity_save_template needs to update the template.

version.description: A version to read (default: the current one).

tools.name: r3_entity_save_template
tools.description: Save an Entity of a project as an entity template version: its members (the components bound to it, with the positions, rotations and colours they hold), a description and a picture. `description` is required (20..1000 characters): write it from the Entity's components and its code, in plain words for someone browsing templates: what it is, what it does when the project runs, and how to use it (what to add it to, what it needs). `controls` (optional, at most 200 characters) names its keys or buttons, e.g. "Arrow keys drive, Space brakes". The picture: after the save, any open R3 tab of the account renders the template alone (framed on it, as authored, nothing running) and keeps it as the template's picture. With no R3 tab open the save is kept and the picture is pending: R3 takes it the next time the user opens the Entities Browser. Without templateId it updates the template the Entity was imported from (or makes a new one, under the Entity's id); asNew: true always makes a new template. Updating an existing template needs baseVersion, the version read with r3_entity_read: if the template changed since, nothing is saved and the answer names the current version. The project itself is not changed. The answer lists every reference a member holds to a component outside the Entity (outsideReferences): infrastructure (scene, world, camera, listener, renderer, transport) is expected and re-bound on import; anything else (a geometry or material left outside) is listed first, because an import into another project leaves it empty. The save is not refused for them.

entityRef.description: The Entity (its entityRef, or its id).

templateId.description: The template to update (default: the one the Entity came from, else a new one).

baseVersion.description: The template version you read (r3_entity_read): required to update an existing template.

note.description: What changed, kept with the version.

asNew.description: true saves a NEW template, never updating one.

description.description: Required, 20..1000 characters, plain words: what it is, what it does when the project runs, how to use it. Written from the Entity's components and code.

controls.description: Optional, at most 200 characters: its keys or buttons, e.g. "Arrow keys drive, Space brakes".

tools.name: r3_entity_import
tools.description: Put a copy of an entity template (this account's, or a public one) into a project: every member with fresh ids, its positions and colours as saved, bound to a new Entity that starts DORMANT (started: false: its code, sounds and physics wait until r3_component_set sets started: true), or awake with started: true (its code, sounds and physics run at once). The copy remembers the template and version it came from. version imports an older version. Answers the new Entity's entityRef and its members' entityRefs. r3_editor_undo takes it back.

projectId.description: The project to put the copy into.

version.description: A version to import (default: the current one).

started.description: true: the copy runs at once (code, sounds, physics). Default false: dormant, woken later with r3_component_set {started: true}.

tools.name: r3_entity_update
tools.description: Bring the copies of an entity template in this account's projects up to its newest version. Without reportId it only reports, per project: what the template changed that the project did not (taken), what the project changed itself (kept, e.g. a moved ship keeps its position), scripts changed on both sides (kept: code is never merged), parts the template added, and parts it removed (kept unless removeGone: true). With that reportId it applies the report to the projects, as undoable changes every open editor sees; if anything moved since, nothing is changed and the new report is returned. projectIds limits it to those projects (default: every project holding a copy). Published releases never change. Applying needs the template:update right.

projectIds.description: Only these projects (default: every project of the account holding a copy).

reportId.description: The report being applied, from this tool without reportId. Leave it out to plan.

removeGone.description: Also remove the parts the newest version no longer has (default false: kept and listed). Plan with it and apply that report with it.

tools.name: r3_entity_assign
tools.description: Put many components of a project into one Entity in a single change, instead of r3_component_set {"entity": …} once per component. Name them in members (entityRefs or ids), or let match find them ({"prefix": "ship1_"} on the entityRef, {"type": "Mesh"}, or both). Each one's value components (position, rotation, scale, colours) follow it, as with r3_component_set; a component in another entity moves (the plan says from where). Without planId it only PLANS and changes nothing: the members, what follows each, what a match skipped (Entities and project infrastructure never join one) and what is refused (not found, a name several components share, two members that would share one entityRef inside the entity). With that planId it applies the plan as ONE undoable change every open R3 tab sees, writing only the entity of each, all or nothing: if anything it touches changed since, nothing is written and the new plan is returned.

entity.description: The Entity to put them in: its entityRef or id (r3_project_load lists it).

members.description: The components to put in it, by entityRef or id. Or use match.

match.description: Find the components instead of naming them: prefix, type, or both (both must hold).

prefix.description: Every component whose entityRef starts with this.

type.description: Every component of this type ("Mesh" or "R3ComponentMesh").

planId.description: The plan being applied, from this tool without planId (same members / match). Leave it out to plan.

tools.name: r3_component_rename
tools.description: Rename a component: its entityRef, the name scripts address it by (this['name'] / this.name), and its display name when that is where the entityRef came from. Name it by entityRef or componentId. Without planId it only PLANS and changes nothing: it checks the new name (refused: not an entityRef R3 makes, a reserved name, or taken in the same namespace: inside the same Entity, or at project level, naming the holder), and lists every Code script whose this['old'] / this.old finds THIS component (a script inside an Entity finds its own member first), with codeVersion and line numbers, plus scripts where the name is ambiguous and scripts that already read the new name. With that planId it applies the plan as ONE undoable change every open R3 tab sees. updateCode: true also rewrites those scripts in the same change (each on the version planned: one changed since refuses the whole rename, never merged); without it they keep the old name and silently find nothing. If anything changed since the plan, nothing is written and the new plan is returned.

entityRef.description: The component to rename, by its entityRef (or its id). Or use componentId.

componentId.description: The component to rename, by its id (needed when several share the entityRef).

newRef.description: The new entityRef: lower case, _ instead of spaces, @ and dots (e.g. "arena_ground").

planId.description: The plan being applied, from this tool without planId (same component and newRef). Leave it out to plan.

updateCode.description: With planId: also rewrite this['old'] / this.old in the listed scripts, in the same change. Default false.

tools.name: r3_module_list
tools.description: List this R3 account's shared code modules: named pieces of script stored once (e.g. "ship-core") that any Code component in any project imports with `const core = this.import('ship-core')`. Each with its latest version. r3_module_read shows one's code; r3_module_write creates or changes one; r3_module_usage says where it is used. See the how-to "HOWTO_CODE_MODULES.md".

cursor.description: Continue a list: the nextCursor of the previous page.

tools.name: r3_module_read
tools.description:
Read one shared code module: its code, its version (the baseVersion r3_module_write needs), the latest version, its notes, and how many of this account's projects use it. Your own module by name; someone else's PUBLIC module by moduleId. version reads an older version.

A long module is read in PAGES (at most 60000 characters each): every answer gives totalChars, the sha256 of the WHOLE code, and truncated / nextOffset. When truncated is true you have only part of it: read on with the same name, the version answered and offset = nextOffset, join the pages, and check the sha256 before you write it back (half a module written back deletes the rest).

moduleId.description: Instead of name: a module id (someone else's public module).

version.description: A version to read (default: the latest). Pass it when reading the next page.

offset.description: Where to start reading, in characters (default 0). For the next page pass the nextOffset of the previous answer.

length.description: How many characters to read at most (default and maximum 60000; 8000 in an R3 Builder session). A page ends on a whole line when it can.

tools.name: r3_module_write
tools.description:
Create a shared code module (baseVersion 0) or write its next version (baseVersion = the version you read). The code is a FUNCTION BODY that returns the exports, e.g. `return { createShip(host, config) { … return {start, update, dispose, api}; } };`. It runs once per run with `this` undefined (it reaches no component: the importing script passes in what it needs) and the same globals as a script (Event, EntityManager, THREE, GraphicsThree). Variables at its top level are shared by every script that imports it; per-instance state goes in what its factory returns. A module cannot import another module. A write on an older version is refused with the current code, never merged. Projects that follow the latest version run the new one at once (open editors reload it); pinned projects and published releases keep their version.

PATCH a long module instead of sending all of it: replacements [{old, new, count?}] with baseVersion and baseSha256 (the version and sha256 r3_module_read answered), no code. They apply in order, each on the text the previous one left; each old must occur exactly count times (default 1), else nothing is saved and the answer names the replacement and how many it found. At most 200 replacements and 60000 characters of old + new text per call. See "HOWTO_CODE_MODULES.md".

name.description: The module name: lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, e.g. "ship-core".

code.description: The whole module: a function body that returns its exports object (at most 250000 characters; comments and readable names are fine). Omit it when you send replacements.

baseVersion.description: 0 to create the module; otherwise the version r3_module_read answered (with replacements: the version they apply to, which must be the latest).

baseSha256.description: With replacements only: the sha256 r3_module_read answered for baseVersion (of the WHOLE code).

replacements.description: Instead of code: exact replacements on version baseVersion, in order (at most 200, 60000 characters of old + new in all).

old.description: Exact text in the module (whitespace and line breaks count).

new.description: What replaces it (empty deletes it). Taken literally.

count.description: How many times old occurs, all replaced (default 1).

notes.description: What changed in this version (shown in the version list).

description.description: What the module is for (one line).

tools.name: r3_module_usage
tools.description: Which of this account's projects (and entity templates) import one of your code modules: per project the scripts that import it, the version it runs, and whether that version is pinned or follows the latest. Projects of other accounts that import a public module of yours are only counted.

tools.name: r3_module_pin
tools.description: Choose which version of a shared code module ONE project runs: version n pins it (the project keeps that version when the module changes), version null follows the latest again. moduleId names someone else's PUBLIC module (it is then the project's module of that name). The pin lives in the project's import map, not in the code: no script changes. Open editors of the project reload. A release (go-live) freezes the versions the project runs at that moment anyway. Not taken back by r3_editor_undo: pin again.

name.description: The module name the project's scripts import, e.g. "ship-core".

version.description: The version to pin, or null to follow the latest.

moduleId.description: Someone else's public module (its id from r3_module_read); omit for your own.

tools.name: r3_blender_list
tools.description: List the Blender models this R3 account has uploaded — one per .blend file name, the current version of each — with what it will produce: how many Blender objects land in the scene, how many meshes and materials, its screenshot, and any PENDING update (a re-upload that changes meshes the user's projects use, waiting for r3_blender_update). An upload with unapplied modifiers is applied in Blender by R3 itself; a model says what was applied, per object. community: true lists everyone's public models instead. Add one (or some of its meshes) to a project with r3_blender_import. A .blend gets here two ways: a person uploads it in the R3 app (Models -> Upload .blend), or you save one you built in Blender with r3_blender_upload (a one-time ticket and an upload endpoint: never a tool argument).

limit.description: How many models to return (default 25, max 100).

cursor.description: Continue a list: the nextCursor of the previous page.

search.description: Only models whose name matches, searched across every model (not the page in hand).

community.description: true lists the PUBLIC models of every user (the Community tab) instead of this account's own.

tools.name: r3_blender_import
tools.description: Add a Blender model the account has uploaded (its current version) to an existing R3 project — the whole model, or only the meshes you name. Every Blender mesh object becomes an R3 Mesh keeping its own position, rotation, scale and origin, with its geometry, materials and textures wired up; objects sharing one mesh share one geometry; a Blender Empty becomes an R3 Empty, the objects under it keeping their place relative to it. A whole model is one Entity whose parts hang from a `<model>_root` Empty: move that Empty to move the model. Reports each object's entityRef so you can reach it with r3_component_set or from code. Use r3_blender_list to choose a model. Pass reparse: true to re-read the .blend itself when the import warns that its meshes were placed at the origin; other projects keep the meshes they use (r3_blender_update moves them, if the user wants). Pass camera to frame the model in a NEW project (its first model: refused on a project that already holds a mesh).

projectId.description: The project to import into, from r3_project_create.

meshes.description: Import only these meshes (by mesh name), each with its own placement. Default: the whole model.

reparse.description: Re-read the .blend instead of using what was stored at upload time. This is R3's Re-parse button. Slow (it re-parses and re-optimises every texture) but it is the only way to recover object placements and flat shading that an older import never captured. Default false.

camera.description: Set the project camera to frame the model, for a NEW project's first model only: refused, with nothing added, when the project already holds a mesh (its camera is then the user's). Omit it to keep the camera.

position.description: Where the camera stands (world units, Y up).

lookAt.description: The point it looks at, e.g. the centre of the model.

tools.name: r3_blender_update
tools.description: A re-uploaded Blender model is always its latest version; the user's projects keep the meshes they have until asked. This tool asks and answers that one question: choice update_projects without reportId shows which projects and entity templates use an older version (or an earlier import of the same file) and what changed; with the reportId and the projectIds / entityTemplateIds the user chose, it moves just those to the current version. Which ones move is the user's choice; "not now" means no call. Parts are matched by Blender OBJECT name: each takes its new mesh and placement; when only its shape changed it keeps the project's materials and the edits made to them in R3; when its materials changed in Blender it takes Blender's materials where the import's own material is unchanged, while a material made or changed in R3 is kept unless the user chooses Blender's (replaceMaterials, from the plan's materialChoices), and a material made in R3 is never deleted. Objects new in the model are added under the copy's root Empty, parts the model no longer has are kept (removeGone: true removes them). Published releases never change. The plan only reads; moving projects needs the blender:update right.

reportId.description: The report being answered, from the plan (this tool without reportId). Leave it out to plan.

choice.description: Required: update_projects. There is no default.

projectIds.description: With a reportId: the projects to update.

entityTemplateIds.description: With a reportId: the entity templates to update.

replaceMaterials.description: With a reportId: material ids from the plan's materialChoices (materials made or changed in R3, kept by default) the user chose to replace with Blender's. Default none: R3's materials are kept.

removeGone.description: Also remove the parts the current version no longer has (default false: they are kept and listed). Plan with it and answer that report with it.

tools.name: r3_blender_copies
tools.description: Does this project hold the same Blender model more than once (two whole imports side by side)? Answers "N copies of <model>: … Keep one?" with each copy (its Entity, entityRef, part count) and its delete plan. It changes nothing: which copy stays is the user's choice, and the other is removed with r3_editor_delete({projectId, componentIds, confirm: {mode: "bundle", planToken}}) once they have chosen.

tools.name: r3_blender_upload
tools.description: Save a .blend you made or changed (in Blender, through a Blender MCP) as the newest version of one of the user's Blender models: the model is named by the file name, so "monster-truck.blend" adds a version to the user's monster-truck model, or makes the model. A tool argument cannot carry the file, so this answers a one-time upload ticket (5 minutes) and the upload endpoint: its URL, method, Authorization header and that the body is the file's raw bytes. Sending it needs file access where the .blend is (the R3 sandbox, or the user's own machine); without it, the user uploads on the Blender page. The endpoint's answer names the model, the version number and its sha256; R3 applies unapplied modifiers itself, and when the user's projects use an older version it asks one question (answer it with r3_blender_update). Then r3_blender_import puts the model in a project. Textures travel only when packed (bpy.ops.file.pack_all()). The ticket states the largest .blend this account may upload (its plan sets it). Needs the blender:upload right.

fileName.description: The .blend file name, which names the model: "monster-truck.blend" (".blend" is added when missing). A name only, no folder.

tools.name: r3_blender_download
tools.description: Get a .blend of one of the user's OWN Blender models (from r3_blender_list) to open in Blender: the current version, or the version fileId names. Answers a one-time download ticket (5 minutes) and the download endpoint (URL, method, Authorization header); the response body is the file. When the current version is the copy R3 made by applying modifiers, the answer says so and names the original upload, with its modifiers intact, to download instead. Another user's model cannot be downloaded.

blenderModelId.description: The Blender model, from r3_blender_list (one of the user's own).

fileId.description: A version's sha256 (from this tool's answer, e.g. the original of an applied copy). Leave out for the current version.

tools.name: r3_blender_draft_push
tools.description: While you build a model in Blender for the user, push an APPLIED copy of your working .blend after each step (body done, wheels done, materials done): the user's Blender page shows it as a 3D preview they can orbit. A draft is not a saved version: one draft per user, the newest wins, kept 24 hours. Answers a one-time ticket (5 minutes) and the draft endpoint (URL, method, Authorization header; the body is the file's raw bytes); sending it needs file access where the .blend is. The draft is a copy with its modifiers applied and its textures packed; r3_blender_upload saves the real file once the user is happy. Up to 20 MB. Needs the blender:upload right.

model.description: The model's name, as the page shows it: "monster-truck" (the same name you will save it under).

tools.name: r3_image_list
tools.description:
List the images this R3 account owns, with the URL to use for each one. That URL is exactly what R3ComponentTexture.url takes, so this is how you find the account's own artwork — a wood grain, a logo, a skybox — and then point a texture at it with r3_component_set.

Search by name rather than paging: search: "wood" is matched against every image on the account by the server, not against the page you happen to be holding.

Each row says whether it is a "texture" (an ordinary image for a material slot) or an "environment" map (.hdr / .exr). Those two are not interchangeable: an environment map belongs on Scene.environment, Scene.backgroundTexture or MaterialStandard.envMap, and renders as garbage in an ordinary map slot.
