You cannot upload an existing image file from here — a tool argument is JSON, this server cannot read your disk, and a real texture is megabytes. A person uploads those in the R3 app. r3_image_create is the one exception: it takes a small image you generated yourself, such as a checkerboard or a gradient.

search.description: Match this text against the file names, on the server. Omit for everything.

cursor.description: Continue a previous listing: pass the nextCursor it returned, unchanged. Omit for the first page.

tools.name: r3_audio_list
tools.description:
List the audio files this R3 account owns, with the URL to use for each one. That URL is exactly what R3ComponentAudio.url takes, so this is how you find a sound the account already has — a footstep, a drum hit, a music bed — and then point an Audio component at it with r3_component_set.

Search by name rather than paging: search: "kick" is matched against every audio file on the account by the server, not against the page you happen to be holding.

scope: "community" lists the R3 Community instead: every sound shared publicly (yours included), with who shared it. A recipe sound there can be read with r3_sound_read and built on.

You cannot upload an audio file from here — a tool argument is JSON, this server cannot read your disk, and audio is megabytes. A person uploads those in the R3 app. r3_sound_create makes a new sound effect or seamless loop from a recipe (rendered by R3, listed here afterwards); R3's music components (Transport, Beat, Pattern, DrumGrid) synthesise music that stays editable and in tempo.

search.description: Match this text against the file names, on the server. Omit for everything.

cursor.description: Continue a previous listing: pass the nextCursor it returned, unchanged. Omit for the first page.

scope.description: mine (the default): this account's own audio files. community: every audio file shared publicly in the R3 Community (this account's included), with who shared it. With a cursor, pass the scope of the listing it came from.

tools.name: r3_image_create
tools.description:
Store a small image YOU generated in this R3 account's image library and get back the URL for it — the value R3ComponentTexture.url takes. This is how you make a checkerboard, a gradient, a test grid or a noise tile and then actually put it on something with r3_component_set.

Pass the image as a base64 data URL (data:image/png;base64,…), up to 1MB decoded. PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP are stored; PNG is the right choice for a generated pattern.

This is NOT a way to upload an image file you already have. You would have to emit every byte of it as base64, which for a real texture is far more output than a reply can hold — and this server cannot read your disk. A person uploads real artwork in the R3 app, and r3_image_list shows what they have already put there: the account's own artwork, where there is some, beats a generated substitute.

Each call stores a NEW image, so calling it twice with the same bytes leaves two rows. The name you give is what appears in the owner's Images browser, prefixed with "agent-" so they can tell where it came from; a descriptive one says what it is.

For a material's texture set (colour + normal + roughness that tile), use r3_texture_create instead: R3 renders it, so no bytes go through you.

name.description: A short plain-language name, e.g. "checkerboard 512". Stored as agent-checkerboard-512.png and shown to the account owner, so describe what the image IS.

dataUrl.description: The image, as data:image/png;base64,… — up to 1MB once decoded.

tools.name: r3_texture_create
tools.description:
Make a matching, seamlessly tiling texture SET for a material: a colour map, a normal map and a packed ambient-occlusion / roughness / metalness map, rendered by R3 from a procedural recipe (seeded noise, stones, bricks …). Nothing is uploaded and it is free. The maps are stored as images in the account (the owner sees them in the Images browser as "<name> · albedo.png" …).

Start from a preset (gravel, sand, concrete, bricks, brushedMetal) with optional controls: seed (another variation), scale (an integer: finer pattern), colours (the ramp's "#rrggbb" stops, exactly as many colours as the preset has: gravel 3, sand 2, concrete 3, bricks 3, brushedMetal 3), contrast, bumpiness (normal strength), roughness {min, max} (from the smooth parts to the rough parts), metalness (0 = not metal, 1 = metal; metal looks dark without an environment map in the scene), size (256 / 512 / 1024 / 2048, default 1024), tileWorldSize (metres one tile covers, default 1), height (also store a 16-bit height map). Or pass a full `recipe` (r3_docs_read("TEXTURE_RECIPES.md") has the format and every preset's recipe). An invalid recipe is refused with the path of the problem.

Pass `apply` {projectId, material, repeat | worldSize (a number, or {x, y} for a long strip)} to put it on a material in the same call (as r3_texture_apply). You cannot see the texture: the answer gives numbers (mean colour, brightness range, height spread, seam check) and the colour map's url; r3_editor_capture shows it in an open editor. Names are unique per account. Each call makes a NEW set; reuse a set with r3_texture_apply.

name.description: What the owner sees, e.g. "Gravel path". Unique in the account.

preset.description: A preset: gravel, sand, concrete, bricks, brushedMetal.

controls.description: With a preset: {seed, scale, colours, contrast, bumpiness, roughness: {min, max}, metalness, size, tileWorldSize, height}. colours: exactly the preset's number of "#rrggbb" stops (gravel 3, sand 2, concrete 3, bricks 3, brushedMetal 3).

apply.description: Also wire it to a material: {projectId, material, repeat | worldSize}.

material.description: The material to wire: its entityRef or id (r3_project_load), e.g. "material_ground".

repeat.description: How often the texture repeats across the surface, on both axes and every map.

worldSize.description: Or: the surface size in metres, a number (square) or {x, y} (its two sides, e.g. {"x": 2, "y": 40} for a 2 m × 40 m path); repeatX = x / the set's tile size (1 m for the presets), repeatY = y / it. Neither given: the mesh(es) using the material are measured.

tools.name: r3_texture_read
tools.description: Read one texture set: its name, size, tile size, the three map urls, the numbers its render measured, the sets it was edited from, and the full RECIPE (the editable source). The account's own sets, or anyone's public one. To change a set, r3_texture_update makes a new version of it.

tools.name: r3_texture_update
tools.description: Change a texture set the account owns: its look (controls: seed, scale, colours, contrast, bumpiness, roughness {min, max}, metalness, size, tileWorldSize, height, applied to the set's own recipe; `scale` multiplies its pattern, so 2 is twice as fine as now) or a whole new `recipe` (read the current one with r3_texture_read, change it, pass it here). The set itself never changes: the change is saved as a new version under the same name (the user's lists show the latest), with new maps, and every project and release that uses an older version's maps keeps them. Give `name` only to make a separate copy under that name instead. The same recipe as the latest version saves nothing. The answer names the user's projects still on an older version; put the new set on a material with r3_texture_apply when the user wants it. An invalid change is refused with the path of the problem. Counts as one render toward your hourly texture budget.

setId.description: The set to change (r3_texture_create / r3_texture_read answer it). The account's own.

controls.description: Changes to its recipe: {seed, scale, colours, contrast, bumpiness, roughness: {min, max}, metalness, size, tileWorldSize, height}.

recipe.description: Or a whole new recipe (format "r3-texture-recipe", version 1).

name.description: Only to make a separate COPY under this name. Default: a new version of the same set, same name.

tools.name: r3_texture_apply
tools.description: Wire a texture set to a material in a project: the colour map to `map`, the normal map to `normalMap`, the ambient-occlusion / roughness / metalness map to `aoMap` + `roughnessMap` + `metalnessMap` (for a set without metal its blue channel is 0, so a metal map left by an earlier set is replaced and the material's own metalness is kept), the SAME repeat on every map, the material colour white, roughness 1 and metalness 1 for a metallic set (THREE multiplies the colour map by the colour and the roughness map by the roughness: a grey #808080 colour would show the texture at half brightness, the default roughness 0.5 would halve every roughness; the colour's alpha, the opacity, is kept). A Color the material shares with another component is left as it is, and the material gets its own new white Color; the answer says which. Creates one Texture per map, or reuses a Texture of the project already on that image. MaterialStandard / Physical get every map; Lambert / Phong / Toon get map, normalMap and aoMap; Basic is refused (unlit). `repeat` is how often the tile repeats across the surface (both axes); or give `worldSize` in metres: a number for a square surface (1000 for a 1 km terrain with 1 m gravel), or {x, y} for its two sides ({"x": 2, "y": 40} for a 2 m × 40 m path), giving repeatX = x / the set's tile size and repeatY = y / it, so a long strip does not stretch the texture. Give neither and the mesh using the material is measured (its own geometry size times its scale, as r3_component_bounds measures; the two largest sides). Kept at once in the project's live copy: every R3 tab with the project open shows it.

material.description: The material to wire: its entityRef or id (r3_project_load), e.g. "material_ground".

repeat.description: How often the texture repeats across the surface, on both axes and every map.

worldSize.description: Or: the surface size in metres, a number (square) or {x, y} (its two sides, e.g. {"x": 2, "y": 40} for a 2 m × 40 m path); repeatX = x / the set's tile size (1 m for the presets), repeatY = y / it. Neither given: the mesh(es) using the material are measured.

tools.name: r3_sound_create
tools.description:
Make a sound (a 48 kHz WAV in the account's audio files) from a recipe that R3 renders: layers of synth / fm / noise / sample sources, each with an envelope and effects (filter, distortion, bitcrush, delay, reverb, compressor, tremolo), and a master stage that can make a seamless LOOP. Nothing is uploaded and it is free (60 sounds an hour for each agent key or app connection).

Start from a preset (laser, coin, jump, explosion, click, whoosh, hit, power-up, helicopter-rotor, engine-hum) with optional overrides {seed, duration, channels}, or pass a full `recipe`: r3_docs_read("SOUND_RECIPES.md") has the format, every preset's recipe and worked examples. An invalid recipe is refused with the path of the problem.

You cannot hear it: the answer gives numbers (peak / RMS dBFS, clipping, silent tail, the loop seam check, warnings), the url an Audio component takes and a listen link for the user. Pass `attachTo` {projectId} to also add an Audio component playing it in that project (a loop loops and plays when the project runs; a one-shot is played from code). Names are unique per account.

name.description: What the owner sees in their audio files, e.g. "Helicopter rotor". Unique in the account.

preset.description: A preset: laser, coin, jump, explosion, click, whoosh, hit, power-up, helicopter-rotor, engine-hum.

overrides.description: With a preset: {seed, duration, channels} (seed = another variation).

attachTo.description: Also add an Audio component playing it: {projectId, name?, volume?, playOnStart?}.

projectId.description: The project to add an Audio component to (r3_project_list).

name.description: The component's name. Default: the sound's name.

playOnStart.description: Plays when the project runs. Default: true for a loop, false for a one-shot (played from code).

tools.name: r3_sound_read
tools.description: Read the RECIPE a sound was made from (the editable source), with its name, url, duration, whether it loops and the sound it was edited from. The account's own sounds, or anyone's public one; an uploaded file has no recipe. To change a sound, r3_sound_update makes a new version of it.

audioId.description: The sound's id (r3_sound_create or r3_audio_list answer it).

tools.name: r3_sound_update
tools.description: Change a sound the account owns: overrides {seed, duration, channels} applied to its own recipe, or a whole new `recipe` (read the current one with r3_sound_read, change it, pass it here; r3_docs_read("SOUND_RECIPES.md") has the format). The sound itself never changes: the change is saved as a new version under the same name (the user's audio list shows the latest), with a new url, and every project and release using an older version keeps it. Give `name` only to make a separate copy under that name instead. The same recipe as the latest version saves nothing. The answer names the user's projects still on an older version (r3_component_set moves an Audio component's url). An invalid change is refused with the path of the problem. Counts toward the 60 sounds an hour.

audioId.description: The sound to change (the account's own).

overrides.description: Changes to its recipe: {seed, duration, channels}.

recipe.description: Or a whole new recipe (format "r3-sound-recipe", version 1).

name.description: Only to make a separate COPY under this name. Default: a new version of the same sound, same name.

tools.name: r3_song_read
tools.description: Read a project's Song: its tracks (each plays Patterns, DrumGrids, Beats or Audio files in clips placed in bars), automation lanes (keyframes on a track's or the master's gain, pan or effect settings), sections, master chain and length, with every source as its entityRef, plus a summary and the songVersion r3_song_update takes as baseVersion. Read it before a change ("move the drop", "a slower filter sweep"). The schema: SONGS.md; the how-to: HOWTO_SONG.md.

song.description: The Song's entityRef; leave it out when the project has one song.

tools.name: r3_song_update
tools.description:
Change a project's Song with small typed changes, or make a new Song (create). The changes are applied in order and kept as ONE change (one undo step, every open R3 tab shows it):
ops: setSong, setSections, setMaster, addTrack, setTrack, removeTrack, setClips, addClip, moveClip, removeClip, setLane, removeLane, addPoint, setPoint, removePoint, setChain, setEffect, addModulator, removeModulator, insertBars, splitClip, transposeClip, setClipGain.
Tracks are named by their id ("kick"), sources by entityRef (a Pattern, DrumGrid, Beat, Audio or AudioPositional), clips and lane points by their index as r3_song_read lists them, positions in bars (bar 0 = the start). Examples: {"op": "moveClip", "track": "hats", "clip": 0, "start": 6}; {"op": "setLane", "track": "master", "target": "lp.frequency", "points": [{"bar": 0, "value": 350, "curve": "exp"}, {"bar": 12, "value": 1200}]}; {"op": "insertBars", "at": 64, "count": 8} (moves everything from bar 64 on 8 bars later); one eighth of a clip a few semitones higher, its length kept: {"op": "splitClip", "track": "bass", "clip": 0, "at": 65}, {"op": "splitClip", "track": "bass", "clip": 1, "at": 65.125}, {"op": "transposeClip", "track": "bass", "clip": 1, "semitones": 2} (whole semitones -24..24; a Sound Studio sound is rendered again from its public recipe, another file pitch-shifted, a Pattern's synth notes moved; 0 takes it off); that clip quieter (a clip's Volume in dB, -24..12, on top of its track's; 0 takes it off): {"op": "setClipGain", "track": "bass", "clip": 1, "gain": -4}.
A song is version-checked, never merged: changing one needs baseVersion, the songVersion r3_song_read answered; if someone changed it since, the write is refused with the current version. A new Song (create) needs none. Every result is checked by lib-r3's song schema (SONGS.md) before anything is kept. How-to: HOWTO_SONG.md.

song.description: The Song's entityRef; leave it out when the project has one song.

baseVersion.description: REQUIRED to change a song: its songVersion from r3_song_read. Leave it out with create.

create.description: Make a NEW Song (wired to the project's Transport), then apply changes to it, e.g. {"name": "Main song"}.

changes.description: The changes, in order: [{"op": "setTrack", "track": "kick", "gain": -3}, …]. Required unless create.

tools.name: r3_voxel_read
tools.description: Read a voxel grid (GeometryVoxels: a block world, ground or structure) without its encoded data: size in cells and metres, cell size, rules (support, crumbleHeight, outsideSolid), the palette with how many cells of each material, bonds, the Meshes that draw it, and the voxelVersion r3_voxel_edit takes as baseVersion. Optional: region {"min": [i, j, k], "max": [i, j, k]} (cells, inclusive; j is up) answers those cells as text rows, one character per cell with a legend (. = air); slice: j answers one whole layer; heightmap: true the top solid row of each column (in the region, else the whole grid). Read it before an edit. How-to: HOWTO_VOXELS.md.

voxels.description: The GeometryVoxels' entityRef, or a Mesh that draws it; leave it out when the project has one grid.

region.description: A box of cells to answer, e.g. {"min": [0, 0, 0], "max": [15, 3, 15]} (at most 32,768 cells).

slice.description: One whole layer j (0 = the bottom row) as text rows.

heightmap.description: true: the top solid row j of each column (-1 = empty column).

tools.name: r3_voxel_edit
tools.description:
Change a voxel grid (GeometryVoxels) with a list of edits, applied in order and kept as ONE change (one undo step, every open R3 tab shows it), at most 1000 per call:
ops: set, fill, clear, paint, layers, stamp, resize, setPalette.
Cells are [i, j, k] (j is up, 0 = the bottom row); a material is its palette name or index ("air" clears). A shape is {"type": "cells", "min": [i, j, k], "max": [i, j, k]} (a box of cells, inclusive), or in metres from the grid's min corner {"type": "box", "min", "max"} | {"type": "sphere", "center", "radius"} | {"type": "capsule", "from", "to", "radius"}. Examples: {"op": "set", "cell": [3, 4, 2], "material": "stone"}; {"op": "fill", "shape": {"type": "cells", "min": [0, 4, 0], "max": [5, 7, 0]}, "material": "brick"} (fills empty cells; "replace": true overwrites); {"op": "clear", "shape": {"type": "sphere", "center": [2, 1, 2], "radius": 0.75}}; {"op": "layers", "top": 3, "layers": [{"material": "grass", "thickness": 1}, {"material": "soil", "thickness": 2}]}; {"op": "stamp", "source": "<another GeometryVoxels>", "at": [4, 4, 4], "turn": 1}; {"op": "resize", "size": [32, 8, 32]}; {"op": "setPalette", "palette": [...]}.
A grid is version-checked, never merged: baseVersion is the voxelVersion r3_voxel_read answered; if it changed since, nothing is written and you get the current version. How-to: HOWTO_VOXELS.md.

voxels.description: The GeometryVoxels' entityRef, or a Mesh that draws it; leave it out when the project has one grid.

tools.name: r3_assets_unused
tools.description: The account's images, models and audio files that nothing uses — no project, no entity template, no other user's project — with each one's size and date, biggest first, and the total. The same report as the R3 app's Settings → Storage, by the same rules the deletes use. A model lists the images only it uses, an HDR / EXR image its preview image: they go with it. A texture set nothing uses is one item (kind textureSet) with its maps under it; a map of a set is never listed on its own. Blender (.blend) files are not part of it: they are the user's to keep or delete, listed by r3_blender_list. Pass `kind` to see one kind, `limit` for more rows (the totals always cover everything). It only reads; r3_asset_delete deletes an item by its kind and id (a plan, then a confirm), for what the user asked to remove. The scan can take several seconds.

kind.description: Only this kind: image, model, audio or textureSet.

limit.description: How many items to list (default 50, at most 200).

tools.name: r3_asset_delete
tools.description: Delete one of the account's images, models, audio files, Blender models (kind blender: a whole uploaded .blend with every version; its meshes in use stay) or texture sets (kind textureSet: the set and its maps, r3_texture_create made it) — the same reference-guarded delete as the R3 app. With asset:delete:created, only an asset YOU created (this agent key or app connection; today: images made with r3_image_create); with asset:delete:owned, any of the user's assets, and only when the user asked for it: pass owned: true for one you did not create (an app connection is then asked for that right). Two calls, every time: without `confirm` nothing is deleted, and the answer says what would go and which of the user's projects use it; the same call with `confirm: true`, when that is what the user wants, deletes it. An asset another user's project uses can never be deleted. A model takes the images only it used with it, an HDR / EXR image its preview image. There is no trash and no undo. Ids come from r3_image_list, r3_audio_list and r3_blender_list.

kind.description: What the id names: blender = a Blender model (its blenderModelId), textureSet = a texture set (its setId).

id.description: The asset's id, as the list tools report it.

owned.description: true when the asset is one of the user's own, not one you created: it needs asset:delete:owned. Only when the user asked to delete it. Leave out for an asset you created.

confirm.description: Leave out on the first call (it only reports). true deletes — after the user has seen the report.

deleteReleases.description: With confirm: also move the user's non-live, UNPINNED releases that use it to the 7-day trash (needs release:delete; only when the user asked). Without it those releases are kept: for an image, model or audio file they are marked incomplete; for a Blender model they keep their meshes (the meshes they use stay). Pinned releases are never deleted by an agent.

tools.name: r3_asset_share
tools.description: Show one of the user's OWN images, audio files or texture sets in the R3 Community, or hide it again: the same switch as 'Show in Community' in the R3 app. public: true makes it visible to every R3 member, who can then find it in the Community lists and use it in their own projects; public: false hides it again (call this tool again with public: false to undo). A texture set is shown or hidden with all its maps; a map of a texture set is not switched on its own (switch the set). Use it only when the user asked to share or hide that asset. Ids come from r3_image_list, r3_audio_list and r3_texture_read / r3_texture_create. Needs asset:share. Videos, Blender models and projects are shared in the R3 app.

type.description: What the id names: image, audio (an audio file) or textureSet (a texture set, its setId).

id.description: The asset's id, as the list tools report it.

public.description: true shows it in the Community (every R3 member can see and use it); false hides it again.

tools.name: r3_bug_report
tools.description:
Send R3 a bug report about R3 ITSELF (the engine, the editor, these tools), in the user's name and naming you (your agent key or app connection). It becomes one of the user's support issues, which only the user and R3's team see. Use it when R3 does something its documentation says it should not, after checking the docs (r3_docs_read) — not for problems in the user's own project, and not for feature wishes (those are r3_roadmap_suggest).

r3_bug_reports_mine lists what the user already reported, so a fault is not filed twice. A useful report says what was done (the tool calls), what was expected and what happened, with what was MEASURED in `measurements` — the values read back with r3_component_read or r3_editor_inspect, the exact error text. `projectId` (when it happens in a project) lets R3 open it. The answer carries the report's link for the user. Rate-limited per agent key or app connection (a few an hour). Needs the support:write right.

title.description: One line naming the fault, e.g. "Cuboid collider with halfExtents.z = 0 inverts the contact normal".

description.description: What you did, what you expected, what happened instead.

projectId.description: The project it happens in (r3_project_list), if any. Only a project the user can open.

measurements.description: What you measured: values read back, exact error text, timings. Plain text.

tools.name: r3_bug_reports_mine
tools.description: The user's own support issues — bug reports and questions they or their agents (agent keys and app connections) sent R3 — newest first, with status, date, the project and whether an agent filed it (and which), each with its link. It shows whether a fault is already reported, before r3_bug_report would file it twice. Needs the support:write right.

limit.description: How many to return, newest first (default 20).

tools.name: r3_roadmap_list
tools.description: The public R3 roadmap: what is planned, in progress, proposed by the community and shipped, with each item's vote count and whether the user has voted for it — plus the user's OWN suggestions still awaiting R3's approval, marked pending, and the ones R3 declined, marked declined with R3's reason (only the user sees them; neither is votable); a declined item is not suggested again. It shows whether an item already covers an idea before r3_roadmap_suggest: r3_roadmap_upvote votes for that one instead of a duplicate. Narrow it with `search` (title and description, any case) and `status`.

search.description: Words to find in the title or description, any case.

tools.name: r3_roadmap_upvote
tools.description: Add the user's vote to a public roadmap item (its id from r3_roadmap_list), when the user wants it or it covers what you were about to suggest. One vote per user: an item the user already voted for stays voted, and this never removes a vote. Needs the roadmap:vote right.

id.description: The roadmap item id, from r3_roadmap_list.

tools.name: r3_roadmap_suggest
tools.description: Suggest a feature for R3's public roadmap, in the user's name and naming you (your agent key or app connection). It is HELD until R3's team approves it: not public, not votable, until then. r3_roadmap_list shows whether an item already covers it (r3_roadmap_upvote votes for that one instead). A good suggestion says what the feature lets a person do and why (what was being built when it was missed). Something broken rather than missing is r3_bug_report's. Rate-limited per agent key or app connection (a few a day). Needs the roadmap:suggest right.

title.description: One line naming the feature, e.g. "Per-wheel tyre grip in the Inspector".

description.description: What it lets a person do, and why it is needed.

tools.name: r3_project_changes
tools.description:
What OTHER people changed in a project — the user in any R3 tab, their other agents — oldest first, grouped per author and per thing: properties set, code and help updated (with versions), components added, deleted or restored, the project renamed. Your own changes are never listed. Every answer about a project already ends with a short "Since your last call" line; this is its full list.

Without `since`: from where you last looked (and moves that mark to now, unless advance: false). The mark belongs to your agent key or app connection, not to the conversation: two conversations on one share it. With `since` (a seq, e.g. the one the "+N more" line names, or 0 for everything still in the log): from there, without moving anything. Needs project:read.

since.description: List from this seq on (the "+N more" line names it; 0 = everything the log still holds).

advance.description: Without since: move your mark to now (default true). false reads without moving it.

limit.description: At most this many groups, the newest (default 50, at most 200); the rest are counted.
